prompt: DNSSEC is on for the public zone, but no resolver checks its signatures. What half is missing?

choices.text: A second managed zone for the signatures
choices.why: Signatures live in the same zone.

choices.text: A TXT record with the key
choices.why: Keys are published as DNSKEY records, which Cloud DNS makes.

choices.text: A DS record the registrar publishes
choices.why: Right. Signing is Cloud DNS's half; the DS record in the parent is the other.
Private zones are not what DNSSEC protects.

prompt: Every name in Cloud DNS is written fully qualified, ending with a ___, as in `planner.example.com.`

choices.why: A TTL is time, not a count.
300 is seconds.

Resolvers are not told about changes; they wait out the TTL.

prompt: `dig` asked for the A record of `www.planner.example.com` and got only a CNAME. What does a resolver do next?

choices.text: Follow it to the name it names
choices.why: Right. The CNAME says what www is; the address belongs to the name it points at.

choices.text: Report that www has no address
choices.why: It has one, through the name the CNAME names.
Registrars hold delegations, not records.
MX is for mail.

prompt: A name was looked up a moment before its record was created, and answered NXDOMAIN. Why can it still look missing afterwards?

choices.text: New records take a day to be created
choices.why: Creation is quick; caching is the delay.
Records are added to an existing zone.

choices.text: dig only reads the zone file once a day
choices.why: dig reads no file; it asks a server.

choices.text: NXDOMAIN is cached like any answer
choices.why: Right. Resolvers keep the negative answer for a while.
